Decided: the test-writer moves an existing test that the on state breaks, by renaming it; nobody edits or drops one. The move carries one of two tokens. flag_old_<k>: a criterion of a story behind the flag replaces everything the test asserts; the test is deleted when the flag is removed. flag_pending_<k>: the test asserts behaviour the product must keep that the flag's stories do not provide yet, which is the half-finished case of clause 2b. When: in the tests stage where the criteria show the need; otherwise after the green gate's run with the flag on (F-ON) names the test, through the existing test-defects step: the implementer changes code only where the code is at fault, else returns blocked with the test under test_defects, and the test-writer moves it and re-freezes. No stage, step or prompt is added. What checks the move. Programs: F-STATES holds a moved test to passing with no flag set and to naming the flag-off criterion, and refuses more missing base tests than new moved tests, so an existing test leaves the suite only by a move; F-ON leaves moved tests out of the on run, refuses a moved test that passes with the flag on (it is given its name back), names every other failing test and says whether the base held it, and refuses a turn-on story while a pending test remains; F-DEFINITION refuses a removal that leaves a test named for the off state. Reviewer: the adversary's item flag-off, which only checked satisfies, now covers each moved test (an existing test, assertions unchanged, old only where a criterion replaces it, no other existing test deleted, renamed or weakened); the item is also added to a turn-on story and comes back in a later loop that touches tests. The pull request body lists the moved tests by name. Walked through red, green and review for a feature added to existing code, for a feature built over several stories, for turning on and for removal. Not changed, and outside this finding: vsdd env start turns every live temporary flag on for wave and release evaluation, which includes a flag whose feature is unfinished.

A token now ends at the end of the name, at '__', or at a character that is not a letter, a digit or '_', so a single '_' after it belongs to a longer key and flag_off_checkout no longer matches inside flag_off_checkout_v2. The encoded form of a key is defined once, in the header of flag-checks.toml: lower case, each run of other characters written as one '_', none at either end. It can therefore never contain '__', which is what makes the terminator safe for every key, inherited ones included. F-RECORD refuses a new key whose encoded form is another record's, and F-REQUIRE refuses a story behind a flag whose encoded form another record shares. The alternative, refusing a key that begins another, was rejected: keys are never reused, so it would forbid 'checkout.v2' for ever once 'checkout' existed, and it could not cover two inherited keys.

'Every gate result' is dropped: config/flags.md now says the line is printed by vsdd status, the briefing and the release packet. flag-lifecycle.md 'The release' says that in the state requested the packet's section is that one line, and that in the state off there is no section. Both have a builder: F1 delivers the states in status and the briefing, F3 the flag lines of the release packet. The helper called from every gate result was rejected: no flag check runs in that state, a gate result is read by a script and not by a person, and it would add a flag dependency to every gate package for a line that has no reader there.

flags.enabled is now set_by proposal with override = true, and its meaning says it is the one key F-FILL does not copy as written. flags.require is the only key left with set_by person, and the header says a proposal that carries such a key is refused (F-CHOICE). The D31 passage of project-configuration.md no longer says what [flags.approved] holds; it links to config:flags, which links to F-FILL.
